Olivia Chow’s Scarborough Rally Speech

Scarborough – are you ready to choose hope over fear? Unity over division? To move forward not backward? Are you ready to win?

I love our city! I love the vibrancy and energy of our neighbourhoods. The street festivals, the food, the music, the people who have come here from every corner of the world.

And Scarborough brings all of that together.

From the bluffs to Rouge Park. From the shops and restaurants along Lawrence Avenue to the families gathering in our parks and community centres. So many cultures. So many languages. So much great food! Part of one city we all call home.

When I came to Toronto as an immigrant kid, I was looking for a place to belong. A lot of you know what I mean! I learned to skate at Nathan Phillips Square. It made me feel like a Canadian. And I loved that it was free. I learned to ride a bike on Centre Island. I spent hours at the Reference Library, using old art books to build my career as a struggling artist.
doc_title: Olivia Chow shares vision for Scarborough at rally - Olivia Chow for Mayor of Toronto

text:
Our city made me who I am today. An immigrant kid from St. Jamestown who became your mayor. And all of my best memories happened in public spaces. Places we created together.

Now let’s be frank, for way too long Scarborough lacked public spaces. Austerity budgets cut the services your families need to get ahead. Not enough libraries. Not enough TTC service. Not enough community centres. But all of that is changing. We are turning the corner.

Scarborough, we are building the places families deserve! I just opened the beautiful new Rouge Valley Community Centre. Have you seen it? And that new indoor cricket pitch? It’s awesome. Kidstown is open again, with a huge new water play area. We need to move ahead with the Milliken Community Centre expansion. And to everyone who has worked so hard, and dreamed so long, for a Tamil Community Centre: together, we are getting it done!
doc_title: Olivia Chow shares vision for Scarborough at rally - Olivia Chow for Mayor of Toronto

text:
Thank you Councillor Shan, thank you Tamil community, because this is more than a place for the Tamil community to preserve its culture and heritage. It is a gift to all of Scarborough. And for 30 years, people in Scarborough have also dreamed of an Asian Garden. Now the shovels are hitting the ground this fall right here at the Chinese Cultural Centre!

And we’re not stopping there. Because the people of Scarborough should not have to wait two hours to get across Scarborough! You deserve that time with your families. In just a few days, the new Scarborough Busway opens. That could give a TTC rider an hour back every week!

And we are putting $18 million into design work for the Scarborough East LRT. Scarborough has waited long enough. Let’s build it!

But what good is better transit if families can’t afford to ride it? Well, we’re changing that, too! We’ve frozen TTC fares for three years. This month, rides become free after 47 trips in a month.

And in my next term? Ten rides a week, then free! More time at home. More money in your pocket. That’s what we’re fighting for!
doc_title: Olivia Chow shares vision for Scarborough at rally - Olivia Chow for Mayor of Toronto

text:
And when Scarborough fights, Scarborough wins! Just yesterday, VIA Rail backed off from cutting Guildwood Station. And we’ll keep fighting to make sure they don’t even try it again.

And we’re fighting for your kids, too. Thirty-five years ago, Jack Layton and I dreamed of feeding every child in every Toronto school. We worked out the cost. We made a plan. We kept at it.

And now, as your mayor, that dream has become a reality! Every classroom! Every school! Every child! Including every child right here in Scarborough!

And yes, we’re building homes. Homes you can afford. Homes for seniors on Sewells Road. New co-op housing at Kennedy Commons. And we are going to keep building, because every family deserves a place to call home!

Things are getting better here in Scarborough. New places to play. Better transit on the way.

Food for our kids. Homes being built. And here’s another thing.

Scarborough is becoming the newest artistic engine of our city. So we need more ways to gather, create, practice and perform. The talent is here, we will support it. We have so much more to do. And we will do it, together!
doc_title: Olivia Chow shares vision for Scarborough at rally - Olivia Chow for Mayor of Toronto

text:
As a city, we are finally, after a long time, feeling more optimistic. We have momentum.

And now, we have to keep that momentum going. Because these are not easy times. Trump and his tariffs create uncertainty and stress. Our world is rapidly changing around us. Everything is less affordable, for almost everyone. Torontonians are doing their very best, working harder than ever before. Sometimes multiple jobs. And our city needs to support them if Toronto is going to live up to its full potential.

So we have a choice to make. We can choose to work together, support each other, continue building the city we love, a joyous city that invites us and welcomes us. Where we care for each other and stand up for each other. Where we celebrate who we are: ambitious, hardworking, ready to win, ready to go forward. Where we build more housing and lower the cost of living. Where we decide our own future. As Torontonians.
doc_title: Olivia Chow shares vision for Scarborough at rally - Olivia Chow for Mayor of Toronto

text:
Or we can go backwards. We could choose leaders who will starve our public spaces, cut and burn and slash our services like the bad old days. Divide us instead of bringing us together. We’ve been there. Done that. We are not going backwards. That is not what I want. I do not believe it’s what you want either.

We want a stronger Scarborough. A better Scarborough. Because Scarborough is one of the most vibrant parts of a vibrant city. One of the most diverse parts of a diverse city. And in the future, one of the strongest parts of a stronger city!

So let’s keep building. Together. Let’s keep moving forward. Together. Let’s keep building the Scarborough that Scarborough has always deserved. Where every child has a chance.

Where every family has a place to call home. Where life is more affordable for seniors and families. Where we celebrate who we are and make sure everyone has a place to belong.

Scarborough has helped make Toronto the city we love. We can, and we will, keep building a Toronto that is more caring, affordable and safer. Together. Thank you, Scarborough!

TORONTO — Olivia Chow will build another 10,000 rental homes through her Rental Housing Supply Program, including affordable homes, on top of those already in the pipeline. Shovels will hit the ground next year.

With Toronto’s skyline behind her, Chow said the people who work in Toronto should be able to afford to live here. Her commitment builds on housing programs already delivering more than 15,000 homes under construction and sets a goal of 65,000 homes by 2030 – and supporting nearly 40,000 jobs.

“If you’re a nurse, a teacher or a construction worker, you should be able to afford to live here. And not in a shoebox – but in a real home,” said Chow. “These projects are ready. I’ll bring them to the first meeting of Council for approval. No waiting around. Because families cannot put their lives on hold.”
doc_title: Olivia Chow to Break Ground on 10,000 New Rental Homes Next Year - Olivia Chow for Mayor of Toronto

text:
Chow’s rental incentives lower the cost of building homes in exchange for affordable housing. It’s also fast: a project must be able to start construction in the next 12 months to qualify. When the first round opened in November 2024, shovels went into the ground just three months later. The next round of 10,000 homes will only go forward if Chow is re-elected.

Chow has also worked with Prime Minister Mark Carney and Premier Doug Ford to secure funding that helps Toronto build housing while maintaining investment in transit, water and roads.

Chow worked with both governments to secure $1.5 billion for Toronto through the Canada-Ontario Partnership to Build. Toronto was the first municipality to receive a funding announcement under the Development Charge Reduction Program. Chow is leveraging this funding to deliver 10,000 more homes through her signature Rental Housing Supply Program.

That partnership provides greater financial certainty to keep rental housing moving during a slowdown. It also supports larger development-charge reductions for homes with two or more bedrooms, encouraging the family-sized housing Toronto needs.

Chow rejects any scheme to privatize water, which drives up costs and puts safety in question

- Facebook

TORONTO - Olivia Chow will build a more affordable city without handing over our drinking water to the province, or opening the door to privatization.

In the final stretch of the campaign, Chow is reminding voters about the stakes in this election, saying she will always protect public services, especially when it comes to our precious drinking water. She was joined by acclaimed scientist and broadcaster David Suzuki and local families at RC Harris Water Treatment Plant.

Today, 16 incumbent Toronto City Councillors from across the political spectrum have spoken out to oppose Bradford’s plan.

According to a new legal analysis, Bradford’s scheme hands over control of Toronto’s water to the provincial government, taking away the City’s power to set rates, decide infrastructure priorities, and making the City powerless against privatization.
doc_title: Olivia Chow will build a more affordable city without giving up Toronto’s drinking water - Olivia Chow for Mayor of Toronto

text:
“There is a lot at stake in this election. My opponent is proposing to give up control of Toronto’s safe, clean drinking water. We wouldn’t be able to set the rates, decide which pipes need upgrades, or even stop privatization by the Ford government. I will never gamble with a public service that every family depends on, and I will never open the door to privatization,” said Chow.

“I have a plan to lower people’s day-to-day costs and make life more affordable in our city. Lowering transit costs, supporting local grocery stores and bringing more affordable food into our neighbourhoods, building more affordable homes, so our children have a chance to build their lives here. These are the things Torontonians are asking for, not privatizing water, which will hurt safety and drive up costs like it has in other cities around the world,” said Chow.

Already, the Toronto Region Board of Trade is advocating for Bradford’s proposed water corporation to be opened up to private investment.

BACKGROUND:

Water legislation and legal opinion:

-
doc_title: Olivia Chow will build a more affordable city without giving up Toronto’s drinking water - Olivia Chow for Mayor of Toronto

text:
According to a new legal analysis of provincial legislation by Goldblatt Partners, the province would have the ultimate authority to set the water rates (making it impossible for any candidate to guarantee low rates), as well as control over ownership, governance and operations.

-

The province would also have control over privatizing water, the legal opinion states:

The Bradford Proposal states that a WWC would be owned 100% by Toronto taxpayers and a bylaw would permanently ban private investment. This is misleading. City Council can pass a bylaw, but does not have the power to change or over-ride the Ministerial powers to intervene in WWCs. If the Minister decided to change the ownership or control of a WWC, they would have the power to do so. See page 2.

Opposition from City Councillors and the public

-

16 incumbent Toronto City Councillors from all sides of the political spectrum have signed a letter against Bradford’s water scheme:

“Using debt to pay for water infrastructure is a bad idea. It will cost Torontonians more in the long run” said incumbent Jon Burnside, Don Valley East.

-

Former Mayor David Miller has spoken out against Bradford’s scheme here. He writes:
doc_title: Olivia Chow will build a more affordable city without giving up Toronto’s drinking water - Olivia Chow for Mayor of Toronto

text:
Yet one conservative mayoral candidate, Brad Bradford — and the conservative think tank backing him — want to turn Toronto Water into a separate corporation. That is the first step toward privatization: an ideological answer to a problem that does not exist. And it is, above all, a really, really bad idea.

-

A poll shows 62% of Torontonians say they are concerned about the possibility of Toronto Water being privatized.

SCARBOROUGH (October 13, 2026) - Olivia Chow will lower transit costs and build the Scarborough East LRT for Scarborough residents.

Just weeks ago, Chow delivered the new busway for Scarborough, which had 60,000 riders on its first day, and the first month of fare capping was a huge success: nearly 60,000 TTC riders got free rides in September.

She spoke to transit riders grabbing a coffee at Ethio Natural Coffee, around the corner from Victoria Park station.

“I built the busway because I am a mayor who stands up for Scarborough. Next I will build the Scarborough East LRT and make transit much more affordable. I have already set aside the downpayment to build the LRT, shovels will hit the ground in my next term. Re-elect me to keep moving forward and get it done," said Chow.
doc_title: Olivia Chow will Deliver Better Transit for Scarborough - Olivia Chow for Mayor of Toronto

text:
“For years, my Conservative opponent cut TTC service and raised fares, which left Scarborough behind. He was on the TTC board when they cut maintenance for the Scarborough RT and then it derailed. We can’t go backwards to the days of cuts and poor service. We know it does not work. Let’s keep moving forward, investing in better transit for Scarborough and making life more affordable,” said Chow.

Olivia Chow will deliver for Scarborough transit riders:

-

Lower transit costs: 10 trips then the TTC is free, each week. Lowering the cost of transit can save Scarborough TTC riders hundreds of dollars a year while reducing congestion.

-

Building the Scarborough East LRT: Chow will get shovels in the ground next term. She has already saved nearly $400 million for a downpayment, and she has expedited design and engineering work. Chow has made it the City’s top transit priority.

-

Continuing to invest in more frequent bus service for Scarborough. Throughout her time as mayor, Chow has invested in increasing TTC service levels in Scarborough. She will never cut transit.

-
doc_title: Olivia Chow will Deliver Better Transit for Scarborough - Olivia Chow for Mayor of Toronto

text:
Keeping her promise to build Scarborough Transit: Chow stood up for Scarborough after the SRT derailed and built the Busway. It’s open and saves 100,000 Scarborough transit riders an hour per week.

-

New subway cars: Chow is buying new state-of-the-art subway trains for Line 2, which will serve the new Scarborough Subway when it opens, giving riders a reliable ride.

TORONTO (September 25, 2026) – Olivia Chow will crack down on slumlords with new dedicated enforcement.

Chow’s Bad Landlords Task Force will lead an aggressive, proactive enforcement effort directed at problem landlords and buildings. This builds forward on Olivia Chow’s work at 500 Dawes.

“Half of Torontonians rent their homes, they deserve safe and healthy places to live. There are too many slumlords who won’t do the basics, they’ve been getting away with it for too long,” said Chow.

“So far, we’ve supported renters by banning renovictions and investing in more inspectors, but we need to keep moving forward. We can get tough on the bad landlords that make life harder for people in our city,” said Chow.
doc_title: Olivia Chow will go after slumlords with a new enforcement team - Olivia Chow for Mayor of Toronto

text:
The new team will consist of enforcement officers and lawyers with a focussed, clear mandate to pursue the worst buildings and landlords, with proactive inspections and issuing court orders for repairs. For landlords that refuse, Chow will ramp up Remedial Action: the City making the repairs and billing the landlord.

“I saw the living conditions at 500 Dawes. Moldy crumbling walls, pests in people’s clothing, and an indifferent landlord. This has to end. Everywhere in our city,” said Chow. “We will take action. I am putting slumlords on notice. If you own even one problem building, we will take action in every building in your portfolio. People deserve to live in dignity, in safe and healthy homes.”

Over her term as mayor, Olivia Chow has stood up for renters. She passed a Renovictions By-law, doubled funding to programs that prevent evictions, like the Rent Bank, doubled the number of RentSafe Officers inspecting buildings, and used the City’s powers of Remedial Action for the first time at 500 Dawes.

Olivia Chow will make TTC rides free after 10 trips each week

Olivia Chow is introducing a 10 ride a week fare cap. After 10 paid rides, the rest of the week is free. Chow will also freeze TTC fares for a fourth straight year.

- Facebook

TORONTO — Olivia Chow is introducing a 10 ride a week fare cap. After 10 paid rides, the rest of the week is free. Chow will also freeze TTC fares for a fourth straight year.

The new weekly fare cap means that after you pay for 10 trips, every additional TTC trip that week is free. If you commute to work every weekday and take transit three additional times in a week, for example heading to a Blue Jays game, going shopping, or meeting friends, you could see $19.80 in weekly savings - about $1,000 a year.

“People are working hard and everything costs more. Your city should be in your corner,” said Chow. “If you take the TTC to work every day, your rides in the evenings and on the weekend will be free. It is simple, automatic, and it puts real money back in your pocket.”
doc_title: Olivia Chow will make TTC rides free after 10 trips each week - Olivia Chow for Mayor of Toronto

text:
Before Chow became mayor, TTC riders had been hit with repeated fare increases and service cuts. She made a different choice: she froze fares, restored service levels and secured a New Deal that put the TTC on stronger financial footing. Chow’s three year fare freeze alone has saved a working couple about $300 in the past year.

Under the new plan, you won’t need to buy a pass or pay a big amount upfront. Just tap the same PRESTO card, debit card or credit card as you travel. Once you reach 10 paid TTC trips in a week, the rest are free.

A weekly cap also means riders can begin saving sooner. If you work from home, get sick or go away for part of a month, you won’t lose the chance to save because you missed a monthly threshold. This will encourage more people to choose transit, helping reduce congestion.

“This election is a choice,” said Chow. “We can keep moving forward, making transit better and lowering costs, or go back to higher fares, service cuts and a city that asks working people to pay more for less. I choose to keep Toronto moving forward.”

Unfortunately, what we've seen in the past three years is more delays, more slowdowns, more promises made that haven't materialized.
